ai.description: This slender, iridescent black snake reaches 40–50 cm. It features a series of small, white ventral spots and a blunt, rounded tail tip. It is distinguished by its highly polished, glossy scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Melanophidium punctatum* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct series of small, white, black-edged spots along the sides of its otherwise iridescent black body.
ai.habitat: *Melanophidium punctatum* inhabits the leaf litter and moist soil of high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Melanophidium punctatum* is a specialized fossorial predator that remains primarily subterranean, emerging to forage for earthworms and soft-bodied prey after heavy rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Melanophidium punctatum* is ovoviviparous, producing small litters of 3–6 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Melanophidium punctatum* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations above 1,000 meters.
